title: Symmetric and Transitive
statementMd:
Little Johnny has recently learned about set theory. Now he is studying binary relations. You've probably heard the term "equivalence relation". These relations are very important in many areas of mathematics. For example, the equality of the two numbers is an equivalence relation.

A set $ρ$ of pairs $(*a*, *b*)$ of elements of some set $*A*$ is called a binary relation on set $*A*$. For two elements $*a*$ and $*b*$ of the set $*A*$ we say that they are in relation $ρ$, if pair ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/7078d187b1ce0690fa4e0a5dac4b9a6327f07714.png), in this case we use a notation ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/e33776c12b1110b886c2b3b8860063bd6b3676f1.png).

Binary relation is *equivalence relation*, if:

1. It is reflexive (for any $*a*$ it is true that ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/bc3a0bfef232965ec28452821d9ab08fffccaefe.png));
2. It is symmetric (for any $*a*$, $*b*$ it is true that if ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/e33776c12b1110b886c2b3b8860063bd6b3676f1.png), then ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/cfc217552b88c13e840fc59501c2a60c23b6ee2d.png));
3. It is transitive (if ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/e33776c12b1110b886c2b3b8860063bd6b3676f1.png) and ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/e2faf9b3b19a369533dbc402f00118160d034ee9.png), than ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/82e31464f277331194858117731fe1dea18d5598.png)).

Little Johnny is not completely a fool and he noticed that the first condition is not necessary! Here is his "proof":

Take any two elements, $*a*$ and $*b*$. If ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/e33776c12b1110b886c2b3b8860063bd6b3676f1.png), then ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/cfc217552b88c13e840fc59501c2a60c23b6ee2d.png) (according to property (2)), which means ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/bc3a0bfef232965ec28452821d9ab08fffccaefe.png) (according to property (3)).

It's very simple, isn't it? However, you noticed that Johnny's "proof" is wrong, and decided to show him a lot of examples that prove him wrong.

Here's your task: count the number of binary relations over a set of size $*n*$ such that they are symmetric, transitive, but not an equivalence relations (i.e. they are not reflexive).

Since their number may be very large (not $0$, according to Little Johnny), print the remainder of integer division of this number by $10^{9} + 7$.

## Input

A single line contains a single integer $*n*$ $(1 ≤ *n* ≤ 4000)$.

## Output

In a single line print the answer to the problem modulo $10^{9} + 7$.

## Note

If $*n* = 1$ there is only one such relation — an empty one, i.e. ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/8891a227c918474e5d76377d4644cd7cc01e1ffd.png). In other words, for a single element $*x*$ of set $*A*$ the following is hold: ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/947c6cf761375432db9bd77796bccc89f1f1546d.png).

If $*n* = 2$ there are three such relations. Let's assume that set $*A*$ consists of two elements, $*x*$ and $*y*$. Then the valid relations are ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/8891a227c918474e5d76377d4644cd7cc01e1ffd.png), $ρ = {(*x*, *x*)}$, $ρ = {(*y*, *y*)}$. It is easy to see that the three listed binary relations are symmetric and transitive relations, but they are not equivalence relations.
statementZhMd:
小约翰尼最近学习了集合论。现在，他正在研究二元关系。你可能听说过“等价关系”这个术语。这类关系在数学的许多领域中都非常重要。例如，两个数相等就是一种等价关系。

集合 $ρ$ 由某个集合 $*A*$ 中元素的有序对 $(*a*, *b*)$ 构成，称为集合 $*A*$ 上的一个二元关系。对于集合 $*A*$ 中的两个元素 $*a*$ 和 $*b*$，如果有序对 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/7078d187b1ce0690fa4e0a5dac4b9a6327f07714.png)，我们就称它们满足关系 $ρ$，记作 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/e33776c12b1110b886c2b3b8860063bd6b3676f1.png)。

二元关系是*等价关系*，当且仅当它满足以下条件：

1. 它是自反的（对于任意 $*a*$，都有 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/bc3a0bfef232965ec28452821d9ab08fffccaefe.png)）；
2. 它是对称的（对于任意 $*a*$、$*b*$，如果 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/e33776c12b1110b886c2b3b8860063bd6b3676f1.png)，则有 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/cfc217552b88c13e840fc59501c2a60c23b6ee2d.png)）；
3. 它是传递的（如果 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/e33776c12b1110b886c2b3b8860063bd6b3676f1.png) 且 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/e2faf9b3b19a369533dbc402f00118160d034ee9.png)，则有 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/82e31464f277331194858117731fe1dea18d5598.png)）。

小约翰尼并不是完全的傻瓜，他注意到第一个条件并不是必要的！以下是他的“证明”：

任取两个元素 $*a*$ 和 $*b*$。如果 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/e33776c12b1110b886c2b3b8860063bd6b3676f1.png)，那么根据性质 (2)，有 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/cfc217552b88c13e840fc59501c2a60c23b6ee2d.png)，这意味着根据性质 (3)，有 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/bc3a0bfef232965ec28452821d9ab08fffccaefe.png)。

这很简单，对吧？然而，你发现约翰尼的“证明”是错误的，于是决定向他展示大量反例。

你的任务是：计算一个大小为 $*n*$ 的集合上满足对称性和传递性、但不是等价关系（即不满足自反性）的二元关系数量。

由于答案可能非常大（根据小约翰尼的说法，答案不为 $0$），请输出该数量除以 $10^{9} + 7$ 所得的余数。

## 输入

一行包含一个整数 $*n*$ $(1 ≤ *n* ≤ 4000)$。

## 输出

一行输出答案对 $10^{9} + 7$ 取模后的结果。

## 说明

当 $*n* = 1$ 时，只有一个满足条件的关系——空关系，即 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/8891a227c918474e5d76377d4644cd7cc01e1ffd.png)。换句话说，对于集合 $*A*$ 中的唯一元素 $*x*$，有：![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/947c6cf761375432db9bd77796bccc89f1f1546d.png)。

当 $*n* = 2$ 时，有三个满足条件的关系。假设集合 $*A*$ 由两个元素 $*x*$ 和 $*y*$ 组成。那么，满足条件的关系为 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/8891a227c918474e5d76377d4644cd7cc01e1ffd.png)、$ρ = {(*x*, *x*)}$、$ρ = {(*y*, *y*)}$。不难看出，列出的三个二元关系都是对称且传递的关系，但它们都不是等价关系。
